plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value minus a small amount, aiming to win only when your value exceeds the second-highest value by at least the bid amount. Since this is round 1 and there's no history, I'll bid slightly below my value. A bid of $35.5 should secure a win against any bid below $35.5 and still allow for a profit if I win.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your value multiplied by 2/3. This is because any bid above your value is irrational (you'd lose money if you win), and bidding significantly below your value risks losing the auction to someone bidding closer to their true valuation. Since this is round 1 and there's no history, I'll implement this 2/3 strategy. 33 * (2/3) = 22.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value minus a small increment. This is because any bid above your value risks overpaying, and any bid below risks losing the item when it's worth more to you than the bid. Since bids are in $0.1 increments, I will bid $30.90.
